requests.reason: Read Config fields and their comments to identify supported configuration choices and weakened or optional behavior. Use these distinctions to constrain candidate obligations before selecting a check.

Identify documented membership responsibilities, transition constraints and historical qualifications. Compare these statements with configuration handling rather than assuming a textbook reconfiguration mechanism.
Inspect Apply, ApplyLog, Barrier, VerifyLeader and GetConfiguration with nearby API comments. Determine which client-visible completion events and limitations warrant tracing into internal producers.

Read FSM interfaces and the opening runFSM implementation to examine command and batch consumption, response handling and application responsibilities. Identify which completion dependencies need the remaining event-loop branches.

Inspect how configuration, per-server progress and startIndex contribute to commitment notifications. Determine the actual inputs and boundary guarantees needed for a possible replication-to-commitment audit unit.

Inspect replicateTo request handling, response interpretation and progress updates. Compare this producer with commitment consumers and identify retry, snapshot or pipeline paths requiring separate follow-up.

Inspect appendEntries acceptance, log-store interactions, commit advancement and response production. Establish what a successful response actually observes before attributing any durability or application guarantee.

Inspect requestVote acceptance rules and dependencies on identity, membership, term, log state and persisted voting state. Use observed branches to decide whether election support merits a separate bounded investigation.

Read configuration state, membership predicates, validation and nextConfiguration. Compare permitted transitions and index checks with membership documentation; leave their activation and commitment timing unresolved until callers are read.

Inspect takeSnapshot to identify the handoff between FSM capture, configuration metadata, persistence and log compaction. Determine which completion signals and failure branches require storage-contract or recovery follow-up.

Inspect restoreSnapshot and tryRestoreSingleSnapshot to sample startup recovery and snapshot selection. Compare recovery inputs with snapshot production and identify configuration-dependent exceptions or missing persistence guarantees.

Read RPC response and Transport interfaces, including optional pre-vote support. Establish documented communication boundaries and identify which delivery, identity or heartbeat assumptions need concrete transport implementations.

rationale: These twelve ranges cover 1,371 previously unattached lines across client completion, FSM execution, replication, commitment, elections, membership, snapshot production, recovery and transport boundaries. The supplied documentation motivates questions but does not establish applicability or implementation behavior. This initial survey supports comparing meaningful candidate goals before selecting a small executable unit. Each range is within the supplied file lengths and below 300 lines. Exact character cost and snapshot association require controller preflight against the remaining breadth allocation of 55,336 characters and 18 chunks.
